thread:
Marcus: Morning — LumenCo reporting a spike of 429s during their weekday ramp today, ~09:12 PST. Dedicated pool 'lumenco-prod' hit saturation and requests queued. Escalating for sizing + repro.
LumenOps: Confirmed. Baseline QPS ~120 steady, but a marketing blast caused a short peak ~2.1k QPS for ~3 minutes. Average request payload ~300 tokens. We had 6 GPUs on the pool.
Ivy: Pulling metrics now. Cluster telemetry shows GPU utilization at ~98% and request queue depth climbing. Autoscaler did not add instances during the peak window. Posting a couple graphs in a sec.
Asha: Can you paste the autoscale policy config for lumenco-prod? short spikes need different thresholds than sustained load.
LumenOps: Policy is the standard reserved policy: min_instances=3, max_instances=6, scale_up_when_util_pct>85, cool_down_secs=600. No burst capacity enabled.
Ivy: That cool_down of 600s explains slowness to react for a 3-min spike. The scaler saw the spike then waited the full cool-down, so it never breached the policy long enough to add nodes.
Marcus: Also seeing an auth error pattern around the same time — some 401 retries before the 429s. Could be retry amplification hitting the pool.
LumenOps: We did rotate a service key at 09:05 but clients were supposed to refresh. Some older clients retried aggressively.
Asha: That would amplify incoming QPS. Two immediate mitigations: (1) increase min_instances to 5 for the next 24h; (2) lower scale_up threshold to 70% and cool_down to 60s. Quick CLI patch:

```
redwoodctl pools update lumenco-prod \
  --min-instances 5 \
  --max-instances 8 \
  --scale-up-util-pct 70 \
  --scale-cooldown 60
```

Ivy: I also recommend enabling burst_capacity so short spikes can consume transient headroom. That avoids 429s while scaler ramps.
Ken: Noted — from account side we'll authorize a temporary bump to reserved capacity if needed. Need an ETA for changes and expected cost delta.
Asha: Cost rough: +2 GPUs for 24h ~= +$X00 (I'll send exact). But it prevents user-facing 429s and support noise.
Ivy: Repro plan for eng-runtime: run a load test approximating the traffic profile (baseline 120 qps + 3m surge to 2.1k qps, token sizes 200-400). Also inject an auth-rotation-induced retry multiplier of ~3x to simulate amplification.
Marcus: LumenOps — can you provide a couple sample request_ids for the 429 window so we can tie logs? You mentioned IDs earlier?
LumenOps: Here are two sample ids: req_20260317_091217_3fa, req_20260317_091219_d72. Logs show a chain: a handful of 401s then many repeated attempts with backoff jitter.
Ivy: From infra logs (snippet):

```
[09:11:02] auth-service 401 token_expired req=req_20260317_091117_b21
[09:11:03] client retry backoff -> 3 attempts
[09:11:15] router enqueue req=req_20260317_091215_7c0 queue_depth=18
[09:12:12] worker accept req=req_20260317_091217_3fa latency=420ms
[09:12:14] worker reject 429 req=req_20260317_091219_d72 queue_full
```

Ivy: That pattern shows retry amplification feeding the queue while the scaler was inert.
Marcus: Immediate action items: Asha to apply the autoscale tweak + burst flag (ASAP), Ivy to kick off repro load and validate, Ken to approve temporary capacity increase if repro shows remaining shortfall, LumenOps to patch clients to avoid aggressive retries.
Asha: I'll apply the CLI patch now and enable burst_capacity. I'll post when done.
Ivy: I'll schedule the load test and run it in the staging mirror for lumenco-prod traffic profile. Test will include auth rotation simulation.
Ken: I'll queue the billing approval for +2 GPUs for 24h. Expecting cost estimate in 30m.
LumenOps: We're pushing an emergency client rollout to reduce retries. ETA ~2h.
AlertBot: Incident created: INC-20260317-LUMEN-429 (severity: medium) — assigned to @Asha, @Ivy, @Marcus.
Asha: Patch applied to pool: min_instances=5, max_instances=8, scale_up_util_pct=70, scale_cooldown=60, burst_capacity=enabled. Observing metrics.
Ivy: Initial observation: queue depth dropped after patch and no further 429s in last 7 minutes during a small follow-up spike. Running full repro now.
Marcus: Thanks team — let's keep this thread updated with repro outcomes and whether Ken needs to finalize capacity bump. We'll close when we confirm no missed windows and client retries are mitigated. :thumbsup:
LumenOps: Appreciate the fast action. We'll follow up with telemetry from our end in 2h after the client update.
Ken: Holding temp capacity approval pending repro results. Will confirm once Ivy posts test results.
Ivy: Repro done — with the old policy we could reproduce 429s at ~2.1k spike. With Asha's changes + burst enabled, 429s disappear in all runs and peak latency stays <700ms. Posting artifacts to the incident.
Marcus: Closing notes: recommended longer-term: (a) pre-warm schedules for known campaigns, (b) lower conservative cool_down for pools with bursty traffic, (c) document retry budget guidance in client SDK to prevent amplification. I'll create a follow-up ticket for docs/playbook.
Asha: I'll roll the autoscale policy change into a config template for similar customers.
Ivy: Marking the incident resolved for now. Reopen if we see recurrence.
LumenOps: Thanks, team. Great response.
